cold_open.hook: Army Secretary just quit mid-Pentagon civil war while Tesla's up 5.5% and the rest of the market's basically asleep.

markets.macro_note: Oil-driven rate spike, equity breadth collapsing, energy stocks carry the load while tech stumbles.

big_story.story_title: U.S. Army Secretary Driscoll resigns after Pentagon leadership rift
big_story.angle: This isn't a policy disagreement—it's a structural collapse of the civilian-military chain of command during an active geopolitical crisis, and nobody's explaining what actually broke.

quick_hits.angle: Trump's 20% growth claim has happened once since WWII—in 1951, during Korean War mobilization; peacetime math doesn't work.
FTC alleges Amazon's been running a hidden ad surcharge scheme—the company that invented 'hidden fees' is now accused of hiding fees on the thing it invented to hide fees.
Mortgage rates hit highest since June 2025 on Middle East oil shock; housing market's now hostage to geopolitics.
Retailers are handling tariff refunds like a choose-your-own-adventure book—some passing savings, some pocketing it; consumer gets the surprise ending.

odd_thing.joke_angle: BBC's running a 'beat the back-to-work blues' piece in August—the most British way to acknowledge that summer's over is to ask if you're feeling nostalgic for it while you're still in it.

yesterday_callback.topic: Mortgage rates surge to the highest since June 2025 as new Middle East attacks push oil prices up
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Yesterday we flagged the rate spike; today it's official—housing is now a geopolitical asset class, and the Fed's no longer the only thing moving the dial.

sign_off.callback_target: Tesla's 5.5% pop while the market flatlines—the one stock that doesn't care what the Pentagon's doing.
